summary: Request access to Cost Model API Grafana dashboards + clarification on permissions for finance-adjacent views
description:
Requester: Rishi Malhotra (FP&A/unit economics)

Request:
1) Grant view access to the Cost Model API dashboards (Grafana) for FP&A stakeholders.
2) Clarify who should have permissions to "finance-adjacent" views (drift metrics, predicted vs observed cost attribution).

Context:
- FP&A is actively validating the Standard Cost Model rollout and needs to monitor drift SLI/alerts and schema-version adoption.
- Current behavior: attempting to open Grafana folder/dashboards returns "permission denied" / folder not visible in search.

Impact:
- Slows down monthly/weekly spend reconciliation and makes it harder to answer questions from exec/finance stakeholders.
- Creates ad-hoc requests to Eng/SRE for screenshots/exports.

Dashboards requested (names as shown in links/mentions):
- Cost Model API - Overview (latency, errors, request volume)
- Cost Model API - Drift (predicted vs observed)
- Cost Model API - Schema Version Distribution

Preferred access:
- View-only (no edit permissions)
- Time range up to 90 days (no raw log access requested)

Notes / open question:
- These views are not customer data exports, but they are finance-adjacent and may reveal unit economics at a high level (e.g., overhead allocation %, drift).
- Need a documented rule for which internal groups get access by default (SRE/Platform/Telemetry/Console/Optimize/Finance) and whether Customer Success should have limited access for escalations.

References:
- Slack: #finance thread 1769311802 (questions about reconciling standard cost outputs with reporting windows)
- Recent support context: SUP-31844 (Console cost breakdown does not match invoice) used drift dashboards during investigation
comments:
2026-02-18 (Allison Grant): Thanks—can you confirm the list of users/groups for access? We can grant via Okta group -> Grafana folder permission. Also confirming whether you need access to the "Drift" dashboard specifically (it includes predicted vs observed series).

2026-02-18 (Rishi Malhotra): Yes, Drift is the main one. Proposed initial viewers (FP&A): rishi.malhotra, laura.bennett. We may add one analyst later. View-only is sufficient.

2026-02-19 (Allison Grant): Looping in Rafael Mendes (SRE) + Logan Wright (Telemetry) to confirm the folder should be visible to Finance and whether we should create a separate "Finance" folder or keep under Eng Observability with narrower perms.

2026-02-19 (Rafael Mendes): +1 to view-only access for Finance. Suggest: keep dashboards in existing "Eng Platform / Cost Model" folder, but add a read-only group "cost-model-finance-viewers". Avoid granting broad access to other Eng folders. Also note the drift dashboard can fire during telemetry lag; see runbook.

2026-02-20 (Logan Wright): Agree. No customer PII is shown; metrics are aggregated. Still, it can reveal unit cost structure—so keep scoped. For CS/support, recommend access only via on-call/SRE during incidents or via a separate redacted dashboard if needed.

2026-02-21 (Allison Grant): Implemented: created Okta group cost-model-finance-viewers and mapped to Grafana folder permission (Viewer). Added Rishi + Laura. Confirmed dashboards now visible. Adding a short note to the observability page on access policy and escalation path for Support/CS.
requested_access: Grafana folder: Eng Platform / Cost Model (or equivalent). Permission level: Viewer (read-only). Users: Rishi Malhotra, Laura Bennett. Group-based access preferred (Okta -> Grafana).
access_policy_decision: Finance (FP&A) and Exec sponsor stakeholders may be granted Viewer access to Cost Model dashboards via a dedicated group. Edit/admin access remains restricted to SRE/Observability owners. Support/CS should not have default access to finance-adjacent drift views; escalation via SRE on-call for incident investigation, or request a redacted view if recurring need emerges.
resolution: Access granted via group-based RBAC. Created cost-model-finance-viewers (Okta) -> mapped to Grafana folder as Viewer. Added requested users. Documented the access rule-of-thumb in the Cost Model API observability page and referenced the incident/runbook guidance for interpreting drift during telemetry lag.
